- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.33 to +0.03).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.40 to -0.50) or after a sharp drop.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; model should not overshoot 2–3 days after sentiment shifts.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently negative over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “sentiment-driven overconfidence.”  
- Lag correction: if true outcome is lower than forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 0.5–1% per day.  
- Avoid “sentiment amplification” — do not scale forecast up when sentiment is positive if recent price action is trending down.
